name: Mebeverine Hydrochloride
sections: White crystalline powder (hydrochloride), very soluble in water.
A second-generation papaverine analogue synthesised around the same time as verapamil; not approved in the USA. First approval/introduction: Introduced 1965 (Duphar, Netherlands).

Direct action on GI smooth muscle (blocks sodium channels and calcium influx), relieving spasm without affecting normal gut motility; no systemic anticholinergic effects. Receptor / target profile: Direct musculotropic action on GI smooth muscle; blocks sodium channels and reduces calcium influx; local anaesthetic effect; minimal anticholinergic activity.
Completely absorbed but extensively hydrolysed (parent undetectable in plasma)
Esterase hydrolysis to veratric acid and mebeverine alcohol, then demethylation
~1.1 h (mebeverine alcohol); demethylated carboxylic acid ~2.5 h (PR)
Summary: Rapidly and completely absorbed; extensive first-pass hydrolysis to veratric acid and mebeverine alcohol. Prolonged-release form allows twice-daily dosing.
Irritable bowel syndrome – abdominal pain, cramps, bloating, altered bowel habit
Gastrointestinal spasm secondary to organic disease
PR 200 mg: one tablet twice daily, 20 minutes before meals
Conventional 135 mg: one tablet three times daily before meals
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Not recommended under 10–18 years (varies by formulation).
Exclude organic disease if new symptoms in patients >40 years
Darvish-Damavandi et al., World J Gastroenterol 2010 – meta-analysis: trend to benefit in IBS that did not reach significance; widely used with good tolerability.
See doctor if new symptoms after age 40, weight loss or rectal bleeding
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
